song_story.overview: This is a love song about refusing to rush. The singer has been hurt before — she says as much, 'we hesitated, we were collapsing under reality' — and now that someone gentle has shown up, she's not throwing herself in headfirst. She promises to come closer, but only 천천히, only slowly. It's a rare kind of K-pop love song: not about butterflies, about pacing yourself so you don't get hurt again.
song_story.cultural_root: 천천히 (cheoncheonhi) — 'slowly' — said twice, once doubled as 아주 천천히 ('very slowly'), is the whole thesis of the song. Korean romantic culture has a lot of pressure toward fast escalation — quick titles, quick commitment, 100-day anniversaries counted from day one. This song pushes back against that, treating slowness itself as an act of care.

verse_1.lines: 눈빛만으로 알 수가 있지 / 어떤 세상을 살아왔는지 / 처음 내민 너의 따뜻한 손길에 / 내 마음이 전부 녹아내
verse_1.literal: Just from your eyes I can tell / what kind of world you've lived through / at your first warm touch reaching out / my whole heart melted
verse_1.context: 눈빛만으로 알 수가 있지 — 'just from the look in your eyes, I can tell' — sets up a theme of reading someone without needing words. 손길 (sonkkil) isn't just 'hand,' it's the quality of someone's touch — gentle, careful — which is why it's enough to melt her guard down.

pre_chorus.lines: 우린 서로 앞을 주저하고 / 현실 속에 무너져 가던 / 이런 나를 잊어가게 해 / 너에게 가는 중
pre_chorus.literal: We both hesitated to move forward / collapsing inside reality / this makes me forget who I was
pre_chorus.context: 무너져 가던 (crumbling, collapsing) — describes a slow-motion fall, not a single crash. 현실 속에 — 'inside reality' — implies this isn't about fantasy love, it's two people worn down by real life who are scared to try again.

chorus.lines: 이젠 나를 봐줘 / 내가 다가갈게 천천히 / 아주 천천히 / 손짓만으로 알 수가 있지
chorus.literal: I'm telling the truth / I'm on my way to you / now look at me / I'll come closer, slowly / very slowly
chorus.context: 다가갈게 uses -(으)ㄹ게, a promise form — she's not asking permission, she's stating her own intention gently. Doubling 천천히 into 아주 천천히 physically slows the line down when you say it, the grammar mirroring the meaning.

verse_2.lines: 너가 얼마나 착한 애인지 / 우리가 지나왔던 시간들이 / 이제야 날 버티게 해 / 우린 서로 앞을 주저하고
verse_2.literal: Just from the way you gesture I can tell / how kind a person you are
verse_2.context: Mirrors the opening line's structure (-만으로 알 수가 있지, 'just from ___ alone, I can tell') but swaps 눈빛 for 손짓 — from eyes to gestures — showing her trust growing, one small observation at a time.

verse_2_close.lines: 현실 속에 무너져 가던 / 이런 나를 잊어가게 해 / 너에게 가는 중 / 이젠 나를 봐줘 / 내가 다가갈게 천천히 / 아주 천천히
verse_2_close.literal: The time we've walked through together / only now makes me able to hold on
verse_2_close.context: 버티게 해 — 'makes me able to endure/hold on' — reframes the relationship's slow pace as the thing giving her strength, not the thing holding her back.

artist_context: BIBI made her name with moodier, more defiant hip-hop and R&B — she came up through Show Me the Money and is known for a sultry, unbothered image. 'Very, Slowly' is a softer register for her, which is part of why the vulnerability in it lands.
honorific_level: informal — 반말, spoken as direct address to the person she's falling for

grammar_highlights.usage: 'Just from ___ alone, I can tell.' Appears twice (눈빛만으로, 손짓만으로) — a repeated structure showing she reads people through small signals, not words.
A soft promise form for your own future action. 다가갈게 = 'I'll come closer' — stating intention without demanding anything back.
To endure, hold your ground. Here it's reframed positively — 버티게 해, 'makes me able to hold on' — endurance as something love gives her, not something she has to survive alone.
